claims.text: RHEAs are intended for high-temperature applications in next-generation nuclear reactors.
A significant positive heat of mixing between refractory alloying elements and Cu creates challenges in forming composite structures.
Advanced characterization techniques can facilitate development of a method for large-scale reaction and stable microstructure in RHEAs.
In situ TEM is an applicable advanced characterization technique for this development effort.
Nanoindentation is an applicable advanced characterization technique for this development effort.
Atom probe tomography is an applicable advanced characterization technique for this development effort.
Advanced characterization provides deeper understanding of relationships among processing, microstructure, and properties.
Understanding processing–microstructure–property relationships can lead to a stable RHEA microstructure.
The proposed intervention can improve the mechanical properties of RHEAs.
The proposed intervention can improve the thermal stability of RHEAs.
The proposed intervention can improve the resistance of RHEAs to radiation damage.
Optimization of processing parameters and alloy composition is required to achieve the desired properties.
RHEAs characterized using the proposed techniques can be compared with RHEAs not characterized using them.

contradictions.description: The intervention is characterization, but the experiment describes samples as being 'processed with and without' characterization. Characterization measures a material and is not itself a processing route expected to alter its microstructure.
The falsification rule requires comparison of radiation-damage resistance, but the listed measurements include no irradiation exposure or radiation-damage measurement.
